messages:
Sara - Support: heads up — acme tenant hitting large number of 429s on dedicated pool after we ran the quota-migration job this morning. customer sees 5-10% error rate and p95 latency jumps to ~2s.

Jorge - Eng: thanks. any request ids or curl we can repro with?

Sara - Support: pasted a minimal repro below from their app (they ran it from a slow region to match their errors):
```sh
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model":"rwd-2b", "input":"hello"}'
```
Response snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:02:10 GMT
x-request-id: req-ACME-3344
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"rate_limited","message":"tenant rate limit exceeded","quota_key":"tenant:acme:default"}
```

Priya - SRE: I pulled metrics from the dedicated pool. There's a spike in queue length for that tenant starting at 14:50 UTC and CPU/GPU utilization is moderate (~40%). Looks like requests arriving faster than instance warmup. Autoscaler didn't spin extra nodes fast enough.

Liam - Infra: autoscale logs for the pool show warmup_policy = slew-rate and warmup window = 300s. The migration script applied a new quota_profile which sets quota_window_seconds = 3600 for the tenant (looks like per-hour) whereas previously we enforced per-minute windows. That mismatch would make the tenant consume tokens much slower but enforce a stricter long-window cap -> causes sudden 429s when burst happens.

Jorge - Eng: interesting — so two things: (1) quota window changed inadvertently during migration, (2) autoscale warmup config is too conservative (slew-rate 5/min). Could be a backpressure cascade: slow autoscale + long quota window -> queue + immediate 429s.

Sara - Support: customer says this started exactly after the "quota-migration-v2" job (deploy-bot confirms). deploy-bot: `deployed quota-migration-v2 to dedicated-configs at 2026-03-17T14:45Z`.

deploy-bot: deployment: quota-migration-v2 (id: qm-v2) applied to pool: dedicated-europe-2 at 2026-03-17T14:45Z.

Priya - SRE: repro steps I ran locally against a staging tenant to mimic behavior:
1) set tenant quota_profile.window = 3600 and units = 2000
2) hammer with 20 concurrency for ~2 minutes
3) observe X-RateLimit-Remaining drop to 0 and 429s while GPU nodes stay <50% due to limited concurrency per token bucket

Sample hammer: ```python
import requests, threading
for i in range(200):
  t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: requests.post('https://staging/api/v1/gen', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer X'}, json={'model':'rwd-2b','input':'hi'}))
  t.start()
```

Liam - Infra: checking DB: tenant.acme.quota_profile -> {"units":2000,"window_seconds":3600,"burst":100}. Historically window_seconds was 60. That confirms migration converted denom incorrectly.

Jorge - Eng: temporary mitigation options: (A) roll back quota_profile for acme to window_seconds=60, (B) increase pool warmup parallelism (reduce warmup window) to allow autoscaler to add capacity faster, (C) add a transient per-tenant soft-queue (accept & queue) to smooth bursts.

Sara - Support: customer asked for immediate fix — can we rollback just for them?

Liam - Infra: I can patch the tenant row now with a hotfix script: `UPDATE tenant_quotas SET window_seconds=60 WHERE tenant_id='acme' AND applied_by='qm-v2';` will push change to config cache. Doing it in 2 min.

Priya - SRE: after Liam pushes change, I'll watch dedicated-europe-2 queues and request success rate. Also add an alert for queue_length>50 for any single tenant for 10m.

(2 minutes pass)

Liam - Infra: patched. DB + config cache updated for acme. config hash: cfg-9921.

Priya - SRE: initial telemetry looks good — error rate down to ~0.2%, p95 latency back to ~180ms. queue length cleared.

Sara - Support: customer confirmed errors gone and thanked the team. They want root cause writeup and assurance it won't happen for other tenants.

Jorge - Eng: root cause summary I'll prepare: migration script used hours as default when unit conversion omitted, which left several tenants with window_seconds=3600. For some tenants this surfaced only under bursty traffic combined with conservative autoscale warmup. Action items:
- add unit conversion tests to migration harness (Jorge)
- add safety check to migration to reject window_seconds>3600 or >600 unless explicit (Liam)
- tune warmup policy to be more aggressive for busy pools and add a fallback to immediate cold-start for high queue (Priya)
- run a quick audit to find other tenants with >600 window_seconds and fix (Sara)

Sara - Support: assigned. I'll follow up with the customer via support ticket and add postmortem link once Jorge posts it. :thumbsup:
